description: Flying emoji reactions — hover a participant to reveal emoji options; clicking one launches a flying emoji across the full screen toward the target's name, visible to all session participants

userStories.title: Inline hover emoji picker in ParticipantList
userStories.description: As a session participant, I want to hover over another participant's row so that emoji options appear inline without clicking a button first.
acceptanceCriteria: Hovering a participant row reveals an inline row of emoji buttons (all emojis from REACTION_EMOJIS: ['👍', '👏', '🎉', '🔥', '❤️', '😂', '🤔', '👀'])
Moving the mouse away hides the emoji row
Clicking an emoji calls onReaction with the correct participantId and emoji
Emoji row does not appear on the current user's own row
The existing 😀 trigger button and EmojiPicker popover are removed
Unit test: mouseenter on a participant row shows the emoji buttons
Unit test: mouseleave hides the emoji buttons
Unit test: clicking an emoji fires onReaction with correct participantId and emoji
Unit test: emoji row is absent on the current user's own row
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill

userStories.title: FlyingEmojiOverlay component
userStories.description: As a session participant, I want a flying emoji animation that travels across the full screen toward the target participant's name, splats on arrival, then fades out.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a FlyingEmojiOverlay component that accepts FlyingEmoji[] prop (each with: id, emoji, startX, startY, endX, endY) and an onRemove(id: string) callback
Each flying emoji renders at its startX/Y and animates toward endX/Y over ~900ms (ease-in-out)
On arrival, plays a splat/bounce keyframe (~250ms) then fades out (~250ms)
onRemove is called with the correct id after the full animation completes (~1400ms total)
Overlay has position: fixed, inset: 0, pointer-events: none, and a high z-index so it never blocks UI interaction
Multiple emojis can be in flight simultaneously without interfering with each other
Unit test: given a FlyingEmoji entry, the emoji text renders in the DOM
Unit test: onRemove is called with the correct id after animation duration (use vi.useFakeTimers())
Unit test: two simultaneous emojis both render and both call onRemove independently
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Can be implemented in parallel with US-001 — no dependency between them

userStories.title: Wire reactions to flying animations (useFlyingEmojis + ref map)
userStories.description: As a session participant, I want every new incoming reaction to trigger a flying emoji animation visible to all users in the session.
acceptanceCriteria: SessionView maintains a Map<participantId, HTMLElement> (in a ref); ParticipantList receives a registration callback and each participant row registers its name element on mount and deregisters on unmount

Create useFlyingEmojis hook that watches session.participants for new reaction IDs (by diffing against a ref of previously-seen IDs); when a new reaction is found, gets the target element's getBoundingClientRect(), computes a random start position distributed evenly across all four screen edges, and adds a FlyingEmoji entry to state
FlyingEmojiOverlay is rendered inside SessionView (not at App level)
ReactionDisplay component is removed — no bounce animation remains next to participant names
Clicking an emoji in the picker triggers a flying animation visible to the local user
Remote participants also see the flying animation when a reaction is broadcast via WebSocket
Multiple reactions sent in quick succession each produce independent in-flight emojis
Participant name refs are cleaned up when a participant leaves the session
Unit test: new reaction on a participant triggers launch callback with correct emoji and toUserId
Unit test: a reaction already in the seen-IDs set does not trigger a duplicate launch
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Depends on US-002 (FlyingEmojiOverlay must exist). US-001 can be merged independently before this runs.
